# ADR-002 · One product, four UI languages (ja · en · zh-Hans · zh-Hant)

**Status:** accepted (Brian, Oct 13 2026) · **Owner:** Product Architect · **Domain:** `domo-ai.com`

## Decision

One app with an in-app language toggle, not separate platforms. Math, figures, numbers and scene renderers are shared; only strings change.

**Strings live in locale files, not as `*_en` / `*_zh` fields in cards.** Most of the text a child sees is generated by the validator from templates: each variant's sentence (`fig_text`, `wp_text`) and every step line (`steps_enclose`, `wp_steps`, …). Per-card translated fields would miss all variants. So:

```
locales/ja/…   locales/en/…   locales/zh-Hans/…   locales/zh-Hant/…
  ui.yaml          app chrome, report, landing, picker labels (lenses, tags)
  templates.yaml   sentence and step templates, keyed by figure type / kind, with {placeholders}
  cards/<id>.yaml  hand-written card text (trap steps, trigger, feedback, grounding), keyed by field path
```

- Japanese stays the source. Cards keep their `ja` fields; `locales/ja` is generated from them, so nothing in the cards moves.
- The validator renders every template in every locale for every card and variant, fails on a missing key or placeholder, and writes `bundle.strings[locale]`. The apps look up text by key and fall back to `ja`.
- Videos: Remotion compositions take a `locale` prop and re-render with the same timings. Fonts per locale in tokens (`font.ja` Noto Sans JP, `font.zh-Hans` Noto Sans SC, `font.zh-Hant` Noto Sans TC, `font.en` Inter), because the same character has different glyph forms in JP and CN fonts.

## Rollout (translation follows review, never precedes it)

| When | What |
| --- | --- |
| Now | Locale-ready structure; every new UI string goes through a key (WO-010) |
| Nov 5 | Japanese only |
| January | Language toggle; ui.yaml in en / zh-Hans / zh-Hant (menus, parent report, landing) |
| After Round 2 review | Card text, templates and videos in en / zh, each with a native check |

Translating problems before the Japanese review closes would multiply every correction by four and needs a native reviewer per language.

## Open question for the founder

For the 中学受験 Pass the exam is in Japanese. If the EN/ZH audience is mainly families living in Japan, translate the parent-facing layer fully and show the child's problems in Japanese with an optional translation line. That halves translation and review.
